_comment: Seed for the Concord instance on thinkcentre, generated 2026-09-29 from the
master build file (~/secondbrain/90-Meta/2026-09-28-master-build-todo.md) and
from each repo's own docs, not from memory.
Status vocabulary is Concord's features.status enum, which is the only place
these words can live coherently:
draft         idea nobody has looked at yet
discussion    specified, not agreed
consensus     agreed, not started
ready         small enough to pick up, no open question
in_progress   being worked right now
review        claimed done, awaiting verification
shipped       implemented AND verified by a command that was run
rejected      explicitly not doing, with a reason
Every feature links at least one complaint, because Concord's model is
complaint-driven: a feature answers a validated pain. A feature with no
complaint is rejected by the API, which is correct - it means the feature
is not yet justified by anything anyone complained about.
lorehaven, stashforge, stashbox-fork and gravity were added 2026-09-29 from their
own ledgers (requirements.csv, SPEC.md, PLAN.md, issues-open.json). The master build
file at 90-Meta/2026-09-28-master-build-todo.md had excluded lorehaven, gravity and
stash as owned by other agents; the owner lifted that by naming them here.

projects.name: Lorebook
projects.description: Tauri ebook library manager. Calibre-compatible: reads and writes the same metadata.db, ports Calibre's filename parsers and search grammar rather than inventing near-miss versions of them. Rust workspace, SvelteKit UI, 14 milestones in docs/PLAN.md.

complaints.title: A library built before the curation pipeline has to be rebuilt, not restyled
complaints.body: M1 and M2 shipped before any identity logic existed, so the library view was built against unstable identities. PLAN.md says so explicitly: 'A library view built before this has unstable identities and no metadata worth filtering by, and has to be rebuilt rather than restyled.' The milestone ordering was correct but the cost was paid up front.

complaints.title: Near-miss Calibre compatibility is worse than none
complaints.body: Calibre's filename grammar and search language are a user-facing compatibility surface. A subtly different parser produces plausible-looking wrong results, and a user cannot tell a bug from a mismatch. PLAN.md: 'a subtly different grammar is worse than none.'

complaints.title: A silently empty column is indistinguishable from a book with no data
complaints.body: The template language's unknown-function case is specified as a visible in-cell error precisely because a silent empty string cannot be told apart from real absence. Every layer below this inherits the same duty: a decision nobody can see is a decision nobody made.

features.title: M3.1 Filename parsers ported from Calibre's own save format
features.body: SHIPPED and verified 2026-09-29, commit 171a07a, tag m3-1-filename-parsers. crates/lorebook-parse with 33 table-driven cases. Conventions derived from what Calibre actually writes ({author} - {title}({series} #{n})({pubdate})[tags]) rather than from parse_name_string, which is no longer public upstream. Five mutations killed, including a rsplit stem bug that returned the extension as the title.

features.title: M3.2 Deduplication with version awareness
features.body: SHIPPED and verified 2026-09-29, commit 0ff3560. Pure decision function plus a table-driven test. The agent's first attempt carried a test named after a mutation it did not actually catch; that was caught by mutating the code and re-running, and the duplicate test was deleted rather than renamed.

features.title: M3.3 Inbox store layer
features.body: SHIPPED and verified 2026-09-29, commit 220752f, tag m3-3-inbox. inbox_items existed in additive.sql with no Rust writer at all, so M3.2's ProposeInbox variant had nowhere to go and every dedup proposal evaporated silently. propose_inbox_item refuses confidence == 1.0 as a caller error, because the schema's DEFAULT 1.0 means 'user asserted this' and spec 3.6 auto-accepts at 0.7 or above. 23 tests pass, Calibre 9.15 interop 11/11.

features.title: Wire the 0.7 confidence threshold that decides library vs inbox
features.body: Spec 3.6 says confidence >= 0.7 goes to the library and below goes to the inbox. No such comparison exists anywhere in the tree. The store refuses 1.0 but nothing yet routes on 0.5 vs 0.7, so every candidate currently has to be proposed by hand. Boundary tests at 0.499 / 0.500 / 0.501 asserting the bucket, because off-by-one here silently merges or splits a user's library.

features.title: M3.3 end-to-end: scan a directory with a duplicate pair into the inbox
features.body: PLAN.md's own verification for M3.3, and still not done: the store layer is proven but the scan pipeline does not yet feed it. Scan a directory containing one duplicate pair, confirm the pair lands in inbox_items, accept it, confirm one book with two sources.

features.title: M4 Port Calibre's search parser and compile to FTS5
features.body: Port, do not reinvent: the search language is a compatibility surface. Includes the FTS5 index. PLAN.md puts M5 (template language) before M6 (composite columns) because the default column set contains composite columns, so building M6 first opens the app on a broken library view.

features.title: M5 Template language with a fixed function registry
features.body: #length and #read_dates must work verbatim. An unknown function must produce a visible error in the cell, never a silent empty string. Gating for M7, because plugins use the template language.

features.title: M6 Default column set, column editor, tag browser, virtual libraries
features.body: Must come after M5. Ordered explicitly by spec 10 for the reason above.

features.title: M7 WASM plugin host, capability grants, event bus
features.body: The gating decision for M8. PLAN.md is emphatic: do not build the built-in plugins first 'because they are easier' - the spec's reason for making them plugins is the reason they must come second. A plugin API only the app uses is an API nobody has tested.

features.title: M8 Built-in plugins: Count Pages, Metadata Backfill, Filename Parser, Action Chains, EpubMerge/Split
features.body: Must come after M7, on purpose.

features.title: M9 Instance sync (lore_metadata) and per-field 'instance suggests'
features.body: Must come after M3: no signals without the curation pipeline.

features.title: M11 reading_state and #read_progress
features.body: Must come after M5. Depends on the template language for the column.

features.title: M12 Tiered analytics with a separate exchange consent
features.body: Must come after M9. Consent is a separate grant from the M9 sync consent, deliberately.

features.title: M13 OPDS and the Calibre sync protocol, localhost-bound
features.body: Must come after M9 and M11. Localhost binding is a decision, not a default - Calibre's own OPDS server is what this interoperates with.

features.title: M14 EPUB/AZW3/MOBI readers and writers
features.body: Must come after M2, which is done.

features.title: M1 window-level check is still untagged
features.body: WebKitGTK does not paint under the current Hyprland session, so the webview-to-IPC hop is unproven. M2 does not close it; the two are independent. This is the one piece of M1 that cannot be verified headlessly and needs a real compositor session.

projects.name: Commons
projects.description: A media platform with consent at its core. 32 specs, 8 plans, ~2300 commits. The differentiating property is a consent clause that every object read must go through, enforced by a test that greps the workspace for SELECTs against the object table outside the one sanctioned file.

complaints.title: A declared dependency is not a feature
complaints.body: async-graphql and async-graphql-axum were declared in commons-api and in the workspace root and called from no .rs file in the workspace. A crate manifest was clean, Cargo.lock had zero mentions, and a grep gate passed - two independent checks agreeing with a wrong conclusion, because the evidence pointed at a different file than the bug.

complaints.title: A deferral mistaken for an obligation kept a finished ticket open for four passes
complaints.body: T-P6-007 was carried as NOT CLOSED for four passes because the handoff treated a named follow-on (the upload attestation test) as an unmet deliverable. The ticket's own acceptance criteria were section 5, and none of the six mentioned upload. Twelve tests added, all gates green, and still 'not closed'.

complaints.title: A test that can be inverted is worse than a weak one
complaints.body: The consent test used a headerless request as its 'anonymous' caller. A headerless request IS the local owner, so owner and anonymous were the same caller and the leak assertion was vacuous - it would have passed against the exact bug it exists to catch. Fixed with an assert_ne! placed before the substantive assertions so the next failure names the real cause.

complaints.title: Grepping a file for a path finds the path in its prose
complaints.body: A spec recorded two missing REST routes. Both mentions were inside comments. A route built on that measurement would have been a second HTTP surface for a feature that deliberately has one, and it would have looked correct, passed its own tests, and been wrong.

complaints.title: Keyset paging had never crossed a process boundary
complaints.body: Cursor's only constructor was #[cfg(test)] pub(crate) and nothing in the workspace serialized one, so the after: field on the GraphQL PageInput could not be implemented at all. The plan assumed a small decode_cursor function; it was a design decision about a type that deliberately cannot be decoded.

features.title: T-P6-010 wire after: into the GraphQL resolver
features.body: SHIPPED and verified 2026-09-29, commit 231f6d3. after_paging 10 passed / 0 failed against live Postgres, and mutation-proven: making the resolver decode the cursor and discard it kills 4 of 10, precisely the four load-bearing ones. The other six stayed green, which is the discrimination that shows the suite measures the cursor rather than the harness.

features.title: T-P6-004b remainder: route rejections_for and speaker_cluster_proposals
features.body: SHIPPED and verified 2026-09-29, commit 8e98ccb. Both store functions existed and were tested with nothing routing to them. Now GET /media/:object_id/speaker-clusters and /rejections through the same media_path() consent gate. Declared in both the router and v1_routes plus the OpenAPI list. interview_route 28 passed / 0 failed, with byte-identical 404 parity for absent and denied objects on both new routes.

features.title: Section 14.1 consent attestation
features.body: The real remaining hole, deferred across three tickets because every upload endpoint depends on it and it is a security boundary rather than a feature. Nothing exists today: no attestation type, no caller. A wrong attestation is an unauthenticated write path, so the spec has to be written before any upload route exists rather than discovered while building one.

features.title: Upload endpoints, once 14.1 exists
features.body: Blocked on the attestation. Spec 4 lists these as deferred pending 14.1 consent attestation and a multipart body limit policy. Two of the three are already fixed by 14.1; the body limit policy is still an open decision.

features.title: WASM sandbox (spec 4.4) and plugin UI extension points
features.body: A validated manifest is not a sandboxed plugin - there is no WASM isolation today and HostApi is a Rust trait native code does not have to go through. The host enforces the declared capability set; it does not enforce arbitrary code execution. Anyone reading the crate as a security boundary needs to know which half they have.

features.title: Client SDK generated from the OpenAPI document
features.body: Last on purpose, so it generates from a document that has stopped moving. The document itself is done and drift-tested against the served route list.

features.title: DLNA subtitles as virtual folders (spec 5420, 3135)
features.body: The next open slice of section 11.2. The event handlers for it exist in content_browse where a test can reach the gate; the rest does not.

features.title: AirPlay and bitcode cast paths
features.body: Deliberately out of scope for the DLNA ticket: no device to measure against in CI, and two protocols would make a DLSA discovery test ambiguous. Worth revisiting with hardware.

features.title: Jellyfin compatibility (issue 2747)
features.body: One of the four deferred halves from T-P6-007, ordered after the attestation and GraphQL because it unblocks the least.

projects.name: Whitebois
projects.description: Community platform with an event subsystem, derived values, visits and reputation. 8 migrations, 13 tables, 9 functions, 16 invariants. 76 tests, mutation-checked 5/5.

complaints.title: A harness that reported success for tests that never ran
complaints.body: 29 tests across three binaries returned early because pool() yields None when DATABASE_URL is unset, and the run still printed '29 passed' in 0.00s. sqlx then records applied migrations and skips them, so mutating 0001_init.sql after it had been applied changed nothing and three mutations 'survived' - a fact about sqlx, not about the tests. The tell is now the runtime: 0.00s means a skip.

complaints.title: deny_unknown_fields does not propagate into a nested struct
complaints.body: FileConfig carried the attribute all along, so a [dlna] block with 'enabeld = true' parsed cleanly, the typo was ignored, and the feature stayed off - no log, no way for a user to tell a typo from a bug. The most transferable finding of that pass.

complaints.title: A global badge award would hit the entire site
complaints.body: ending_an_event_only_awards_to_its_own_participants exists to catch exactly this: the award function scores event_count as 'events ever joined', so a fourth user joining a different event would have been scored as if they attended. The mutation is the proof the test is real.

features.title: Spec 20.1 complete, 12 of 12 items
features.body: SHIPPED 2026-09-28, HEAD 7c086c4, tag v0.3.0-event-lifecycle. 76 tests, schema check clean, mutation check 5 killed / 0 survived, mirrored to ~/code/rust/whitebois with trees byte-identical apart from gitignored build artifacts.

features.title: Untangle the 12 pre-existing clippy warnings
features.body: Deliberately left alone at the end of the last pass: outside section 20.1, and a milestone that mixes a new feature with unrelated cleanup is one nobody can bisect. This is its own ticket now.

projects.name: FicNexus
projects.description: Fanfiction discovery and search. Active, last commit 2026-09-27. No plan file surveyed yet - the next thing needed is a status survey like the one commons got.

complaints.title: No surveyed plan, so no one knows what is finished
complaints.body: Every other active project in the master build file has a docs/PLAN.md or a vault spec that can be read. This one does not, which means the only way to answer 'is it done' is to read the code, and nobody has. The first deliverable should be a survey, not a feature.

features.title: Status survey: what exists, what is specified, what is missing
features.body: Read the code, not a status line. The 2026-09-26 audit found two repos 'documented as done' that were not, in opposite directions, so every claim needs a file:line. Output is a table with a definition of done per open item.

projects.name: Threadlight
projects.description: Comment subsystem and frontend, mirrored on gaming-pc and thinkcentre. Last commit 2026-09-27 on both. The 2026-09-26 audit found a 722-line comment subsystem sitting untracked, one git clean from gone.

complaints.title: A 722-line comment subsystem was sitting untracked
complaints.body: Found by the 2026-09-26 audit. An uncommitted tree is not a backup, and this one was one git clean away from total loss. The tree was surveyed and committed later, but the exposure was real and it is the reason the whole master build file exists.

complaints.title: Two mirrors, one canonical, no verified sync
complaints.body: The repo exists on both gaming-pc and the thinkcentre pool. Whether the two agree is not established, and a mirror that has silently diverged is worse than no mirror because it looks like a backup.

features.title: Verify the two mirrors are actually in sync
features.body: Compare the two HEADs and, if they differ, diff the trees rather than trusting either log. Cheap to check and it is the difference between a backup and a coincidence.

projects.name: Streakforge
projects.description: Habit and streak tracking. Last commit 2026-09-27. The 2026-09-26 audit found 77 files staged as deleted here.

complaints.title: 77 files were staged as deleted at survey time
complaints.body: Found by the 2026-09-26 audit and not yet explained. A staged deletion is a decision someone made and did not finish; until it is resolved the tree is ambiguous about intent.

features.title: Resolve the 77 staged deletions
features.body: Either they were intentional and should be committed, or they were an accident that should be reverted. Both are one command; leaving them staged is the only option with no meaning.

complaints.title: A progress document is not evidence that the code works
complaints.body: lorehaven keeps docs/requirements.csv with a status column and an evidence column per row, precisely because a claim of completion is worthless without a command behind it. The three implemented grades distinguish a fully-tested row from a locally-tested one from one verified end to end, and they are not interchangeable: 289 rows are fully tested, 193 are tested locally, and 116 are verified E2E.

complaints.title: Three milestones hold 76 of the 78 outstanding requirements

projects.name: StashForge
projects.description: A fork of stashapp/stash turned into one binary that is a private library manager and a self-governed public curation site at once. Media never leaves the owner's host; the metadata is a shared commons that contributes by default and opts out per library, and who may change it is decided by quorum or moderators, never by an owner override. Plus a P2P downloader plugin (BitTorrent + ed2k over Kademlia). Tracked in docs/requirements.csv, R001-R073.

complaints.title: The ledger says 9 of 73 requirements are done, and the two columns that disagree are the ones that matter
complaints.body: R001-R006 are 'shipped' and R007-R009 are 'tested'. The rest are 'specified', which is the honest state of a project whose plan is written per-step. The gap between 'specified' and 'tested' is where this project actually lives.

complaints.title: A fork inherits upstream's tests, and an inherited test suite measures the wrong thing
complaints.body: The base is stashapp/stash develop at b6b09dd5. Upstream's tests assert upstream's behaviour; the whole point of the fork is to differ. Every milestone here has to be judged by a test that fails against the base.

complaints.title: Governance on top of upstream's models duplicates what upstream already has
complaints.body: The sibling stash-box fork carries 4,480 lines of native edit/vote consensus. Porting a parallel proposal/ballot system onto an archive that already has one produces a fork of a different product.

features.title: R001: Fork of upstream stash with local private library
features.body: Ledger R001, thread foundation. Priority M4. Spec §1. Ledger status: shipped. Built and shipped. Baseline recorded in BASELINE.md

features.title: R002: Users sessions invite keys rate limiting auth migration
features.body: Ledger R002, thread foundation. Priority M1. Spec §9. Ledger status: shipped. Users table plus argon2id; legacy hashPassword not used

features.title: R003: Edit proposals with per-field values and typed ballots

projects.name: Stash-box fork (federated discovery mesh)
projects.description: Fork of github.com/stashapp/stash-box, pinned at b4b8aef2. A federated mesh of independently operated metadata instances: catalog everything, curate together, discover everywhere, preserve forever. Metadata-first, discovery-first, preservation-first, with preservation automatic by default (a scene on three instances unless configured otherwise) and trust unlocking content. Direction decided 2026-09-29: the mesh is the destination, upstreamable fixes are a standing constraint, a running instance is the prerequisite.

complaints.title: A fork with no stated product direction is a clone that will drift
complaints.body: SPEC §6 recorded the open question and four candidate directions (A port StashForge governance, B upstream contributions, C private instance, D other). §6.1 then decided it: C is the prerequisite, B is a constraint on how work is shaped, and the destination is the mesh. That decision is why the phases below exist and why the issue backlog is finite.

complaints.title: Two of the upstream repo's own documented claims were false on this host
complaints.body: SPEC §2 says every fact was measured on the clone rather than taken from the README or CLAUDE.md, and records where the two disagree — two claims are false. A fork built on documentation rather than measurement starts from a wrong baseline.

complaints.title: Preservation by default is a promise the current architecture cannot keep
complaints.body: §7.3 says a scene should exist on at least three instances unless configured otherwise. There is no replication code in the tree, so the default is currently a promise rather than a behaviour, and a promise nobody has measured is a promise that will be broken quietly.

features.title: Upstream issue backlog: 177 open (48 help-wanted)
features.body: Tracked in docs/track/issues-open.json, harvested 2026-09-26. 125 enhancement, 48 help wanted, 4 unlabelled. These are upstream's issues, not this fork's requirements, and they are the stated prerequisite: each is a bounded, provable defect that leaves the tree in a state worth building the mesh on top of. Individual issues are not expanded here — a survey decides which matter.

projects.name: Gravity
projects.description: Federated, self-hostable social platform for fiction and fandom. Rust + SvelteKit, Postgres. No engagement-tuned algorithms, no engagement metrics shown to authors, no ads. The product spec is docs/spec/SPEC.md (3,982 lines) and it is the authority — section numbers are cited in code comments and tests. Mirrored to ForgeJo and GitHub with a deliberate five-topic difference that is a platform limit, not drift.

complaints.title: A handoff that contradicts itself is worse than no handoff
complaints.body: The file's own CURRENT STATE banner records a correction: an earlier note ended 'the Phase-19 T65-T68 hook exists. That was false. feed_builder.rs was a 15-line stub. It was caught by verifying against the tree rather than against the line, which is the only reason it was caught.

complaints.title: A key is not an address
complaints.body: fetch_remote() took a did:key and nothing could say where to fetch from — no column in the schema held a base_url. The function could not be implemented, and the reason was not in the ticket list.

complaints.title: A number that does not reconcile is a number nobody measured
complaints.body: The handoff reconciles 1486 workspace tests against 1005 in the db crate by checking that server --test api moved 168 to 178, exactly the 10 new tests. It notes this repo has hit the does-not-add-up case three times. Agreeing totals are the only free signal that both numbers were real.

features.title: Ticket work T1-T96 (87 recorded done)
features.body: gravity works in numbered tickets rather than one feature per row. The handoff explicitly marks 9 as DONE with commit hashes, and names the highest ticket referenced as T96. Individual tickets are not expanded here; a survey should read the handoff's own audit trail. What is recorded below is the state that document states, not a fresh measurement.

features.title: build_theme_vector() — the one deliberately unfinished stub
features.body: Returns None, so Jaccard remains the live path. The handoff's reasoning is that §14.16b calls the vector an optimization, not a requirement, and names Jaccard as the universal fallback, so the system is correct without it. It does need pgvector plus an embedder, and there is no embedding storage anywhere in the schema. That is a feature with a model-version story behind it, not a query to write.

features.title: §14.16d disclosure gradient (open / structural / none)
features.body: Implemented and load-bearing: an instance must be able to auto-federate WITHOUT disclosing themes that are kink, explicit or political. The privacy requirement turned out to be the same mechanism as the signature requirement — a document is only as private as its signature, so fixing the fake signature is what makes coarse disclosure safe. The three views publish tag names plus a theme vector, per-tier counts only, or nothing.

features.title: instance_endpoints: where a remote instance lives
features.body: fetch_remote() was blocked on something the ticket list never mentioned: its only argument was a remote_instance_did, and a did:key is a key, not an address. instance_endpoints now holds (DID, base_url) per local instance, admin-supplied and never inferred from a key, with address changes recorded in federation_endpoint_history. The fetcher itself is public-IP-only, DNS-rebinding-closed by connecting to the checked literal address, redirect-per-hop re-checked, with a total deadline and no proxy.
